name: Washing hair every few weeks
what_people_do: Keep a style in for weeks and wash only now and then, often once every two to four weeks, longer in braids or weaves.
why_they_say_it_works: Frequent washing dries the hair and undoes styles; the scalp "does not get dirty".

documented_by.source: Hair grooming practices of women of African descent in London, 2016, J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol, PMID 27038251
documented_by.quote_or_summary: London, 242 women of African descent: mean wash interval 17.9 days, 32.8 days in braids or weaves.

documented_by.source: Hair care practices and hair parameters in African American and Caucasian women, 2015, J Cosmet Dermatol, PMID 26300276
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Case-control: African American and Caucasian women differed significantly in washing frequency and relaxer use.

evidence.finding: Descriptive; the authors say some practices are adverse and should be borne in mind when treating scalp disorders.

source.name: Hair grooming practices of women of African descent in London, 2016, J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol, PMID 27038251

evidence.tested: Scalp disease from long wash gaps
evidence.finding: A 2026 consensus (Callender, PMID 41998807) says certain hair-care practices common in high-curl hair may contribute to seborrhoeic dermatitis; the practice named was not in the excerpt I read.

source.name: agent4-traditional-practices.md, 12 Nov 2026 (research file in this project)

harm_note: Long gaps may let scalp disease build up; the exact interval has no tested threshold I found.
